title: Laws and punishments
about: Collocations for talking about laws, rules and courts: verbs that go with law (obey, break, pass, enforce the law), verbs that go with rules and regulations (follow, bend, comply with), and court phrases such as appear in court, reach a verdict and face a heavy fine.

items.pattern: obey / observe the law · observe is formal · a law-abiding citizen = someone who obeys the law
items.meaning: do what the law says
items.example: My grandad has **obeyed the law** all his life. He's never even had a parking ticket.
more: Most drivers **obey the law** and slow down near schools.
Every company must **observe the law** on working hours.
items.watchOut: Obey — без прийменника: obey the law, не obey to the law. Observe тут означає «дотримуватися», а не «спостерігати», і звучить офіційно; у розмові частіше кажуть obey або follow the law.

items.pattern: break the law · break – broke – broken · formal: violate / breach the law
items.meaning: do something that the law does not allow
items.example: You're **breaking the law** if you drive without insurance.
more: The café **broke the law** by putting tables on the pavement without permission.
Companies that **break the law** on recycling can be fined.
items.watchOut: «Порушити закон» — break the law (офіційно — violate або breach the law). Disturb тут не підходить: disturb — турбувати, заважати (disturb the neighbours).

items.pattern: introduce / pass a (new) law (on sth / that… / banning sth) · a law is introduced / passed · also bring in a law
items.meaning: make a new law exist; parliament passes a law when it votes to approve it
items.example: The city has **introduced a law** that keeps cars out of the centre on Sundays.
more: The law **was passed** after months of debate.
Our town wants to **introduce a law** banning fireworks after 11 p.m.
items.watchOut: «Прийняти закон» — pass a law, не take a law. Accept a law зазвичай означає «погодитися із законом», а не ухвалити його. Introduce тут — «запровадити», а не «познайомити».

items.pattern: act / stay within the law · formal · opposite: act outside the law
items.meaning: do only what the law allows
items.example: The bank says it **acted within the law** when it closed my aunt's account.
more: People have the right to march through the town, as long as they **act within the law**.
We asked a solicitor to make sure we were **acting within the law**.
items.watchOut: «В межах закону», «в рамках закону» — within the law, не in the frames of the law. Можна сказати й within the limits of the law, але коротко — within the law.

items.pattern: uphold / enforce the law / the rules · enforce: make people obey it · uphold: support and protect it (judges, courts, the police)
items.meaning: make sure that the law is obeyed
items.uk: забезпечувати дотримання закону; стояти на сторожі закону
items.example: The council employs wardens to **enforce the law** on litter in parks.
more: The new police chief promised to **uphold the law** fairly in every part of the city.
Ticket inspectors **enforce the rules** on trains and buses.
items.watchOut: Enforce — не force: force sb to do sth — «змусити когось», а force the law так не кажуть. Uphold — одним словом; hold up — це «затримати» або «пограбувати».

items.pattern: respect the law · have (no) respect for the law · lose respect for the law
items.meaning: believe that the law is important and should be obeyed
items.example: Most football fans **respect the law**; only a few cause trouble.
more: If people see politicians breaking the rules, they lose **respect for the law**.
Young people are more likely to **respect the law** if they understand why it exists.
items.watchOut: «Повага до закону» — respect for the law, з прийменником for. Respect to the law — калька з «повага до».

items.pattern: the law / the rules forbid / prohibit sth · forbid sb to do sth · prohibit sb from doing sth · prohibit is more formal
items.meaning: says that something is not allowed
items.example: The law **prohibits** selling alcohol to anyone under 18.
more: The rules at the campsite **forbid** fires after 10 p.m.
The new rules **prohibit** cyclists **from** riding on the pavement.
items.watchOut: Prohibit sb from doing sth: prohibit people from parking, не prohibit people to park. Forbid буває і з to: forbid sb to do sth. Deny і refuse тут не підходять: deny — заперечувати, refuse — відмовлятися.

items.pattern: the rules permit / allow sb to do sth · sth is (not) permitted / allowed · permit is more formal
items.meaning: say that something is OK to do
items.example: The rules **allow** each passenger **to** take one bag on board.
more: Our school doesn't **permit** students **to** leave the grounds at lunchtime.
Picnics are **allowed** in the park, but barbecues aren't.
items.watchOut: Allow / permit sb to do sth — з to; let sb do sth — без to: The rules let us bring guests. Give sb to do sth — калька з «дати комусь зробити».

items.pattern: rules / regulations / a law apply to sb / sth · apply – applied
items.meaning: are meant for a person or group and affect them
items.example: The new speed limit **applies to** all roads near schools.
more: Do the new rules **apply to** part-time staff too?
The discount only **applies to** children under twelve.
items.watchOut: «Стосуватися», «поширюватися на» — apply to, не touch і не concern to (concern — без прийменника: This concerns everyone). У розмові буває й the same rules apply for everyone, але основний варіант — apply to. Apply for — інше: подавати заявку (apply for a job).

items.pattern: follow / obey / keep to the rules · stick to the rules (informal)
items.meaning: do what the rules say
items.example: If everyone **follows the rules**, the game is more fun.
more: The kids **followed the rules** and left their phones in a box before the exam.
Our building has strict rules about noise, and most neighbours **follow** them.
items.watchOut: «Дотримуватися правил», «виконувати правила» — follow / obey / keep to the rules, не hold і не fulfil the rules. Fulfil кажуть про вимоги чи обіцянку: fulfil the requirements, fulfil a promise.

items.pattern: regulations / the rules / a contract require / stipulate that… · require sb to do sth · stipulate is formal
items.meaning: officially say that something must be done
items.example: Fire regulations **require** all hotels **to** have a smoke alarm in every room.
more: Our tenancy agreement **stipulates that** the flat must be cleaned before we leave.
The rules **require** dog owners **to** keep their dogs on a lead in the park.
items.watchOut: «Правила передбачають, що…» — the rules require / stipulate that…, не foresee і не predict (це «передбачати майбутнє»). Require sb to do sth — з to. Наголос у stipulate — на першому складі.

items.pattern: comply with the regulations / the rules / the law · formal · comply – complied
items.meaning: do what the rules or laws officially say
items.example: All toys sold in the shop must **comply with the safety regulations**.
more: The landlord had to fit new windows to **comply with** fire **regulations**.
Any company that fails to **comply with the law** can be fined.
items.watchOut: Comply — з прийменником with: comply with the rules, не comply the rules; comply to носії зазвичай вважають помилкою. «Відповідати вимогам» — comply with / meet the regulations, не answer the regulations.

items.pattern: bend the rules (for sb) · informal · bend – bent – bent
items.meaning: allow something that is not quite within the rules, usually because it isn't important
items.uk: трохи відступити від правил, зробити виняток
items.example: The waiter **bent the rules** and served us breakfast at half past eleven.
more: Most teachers will **bend the rules** a little if you have a good reason.
The hotel **bent the rules** for us and let us check in at ten in the morning.
items.watchOut: Bend the rules — відступити від правил трохи, у дрібниці й зазвичай з добрих намірів; break the rules — просто порушити. Fold і turn з rules не вживають.

items.pattern: carry out / conduct an investigation (into sth) · the police / the council / a company carry out an investigation
items.meaning: officially try to find out the facts about a crime, an accident or a problem
items.example: The council is **carrying out an investigation into** the flooding on our street.
more: The police **carried out an investigation** after several bikes went missing from the station.
The airline will **carry out an investigation** into why our flight was cancelled.
items.watchOut: «Провести розслідування» — carry out / conduct an investigation. Make an investigation трапляється рідко, природніше carry out або conduct. Розслідування чого — investigation into sth.

items.pattern: appear in court (charged with sth / as a witness) · appear before a judge
items.meaning: be present in a court because you are accused of a crime or have to give evidence
items.uk: постати перед судом; з'явитися в суді
items.example: The driver will **appear in court** next month, charged with dangerous driving.
more: My neighbour had to **appear in court** as a witness after the accident.
Famous people who **appear in court** always attract photographers.
items.watchOut: Зазвичай appear in court — з in. Go to court — «звернутися до суду», «судитися»: We went to court over the fence. Appear тут — «з'явитися», а не «здаватися».

items.pattern: go on trial (for sth) · be on trial · stand trial (formal)
items.meaning: start being judged in a court
items.example: A local businessman **went on trial** today, accused of not paying his taxes.
more: The couple will **go on trial** in May **for** selling fake designer bags.
He's been **on trial** for three weeks, and the jury will decide soon.
items.watchOut: Про людину кажуть go on trial (for sth): She went on trial for fraud. Go to trial частіше кажуть про справу: The case will go to trial in May. «Його зараз судять» — he's on trial.

items.pattern: reach / return a verdict · the jury reaches a verdict (of guilty / not guilty)
items.meaning: (of a jury) decide whether someone is guilty or not
items.example: After two days, the jury **reached a verdict** of not guilty.
more: The judge told the jury to take as long as they needed to **reach a verdict**.
Reporters waited outside the court all day for the jury to **reach a verdict**.
items.watchOut: «Винести вердикт» — reach / return a verdict, не take і не make a verdict. Verdict — рішення присяжних (винен чи ні); sentence — вирок, тобто покарання, яке потім призначає суддя.

items.pattern: a fair trial · get / receive a fair trial · the right to a fair trial
items.meaning: a court case in which the accused person is treated equally and honestly
items.example: Everyone who comes to court deserves **a fair trial**, rich or poor.
more: Her lawyer worried she wouldn't get **a fair trial** in her small home town, where everyone knew her.
The court gave him a free lawyer so that he could have **a fair trial**.
items.watchOut: «Справедливий суд» — a fair trial, не an honest trial. Trial — сам судовий процес; court — суд як установа чи зала.

items.pattern: be severely / harshly punished (for sth) · punish sb severely
items.meaning: be given a very serious punishment
items.example: Drivers who leave the scene of an accident are **severely punished** in most countries.
more: Companies that dump rubbish in rivers should be **severely punished**.
The players were **severely punished** for fighting during the match.
items.watchOut: «Суворо покарати» — punish severely / harshly, не strongly. Strict зазвичай кажуть про правила й людей: strict rules, a strict teacher.

items.pattern: pay / face / get a heavy fine (for sth) · also a big / large / hefty fine
items.meaning: pay, or be likely to have to pay, a large amount of money as a punishment
items.uk: заплатити великий штраф; (комусь) загрожує великий штраф
items.example: If you leave your rubbish next to the bins, you could **face a heavy fine**.
more: The shop had to **pay a heavy fine** for selling cigarettes to teenagers.
Anyone caught fishing without a licence will **face a heavy fine**.
items.watchOut: «Великий штраф» — a heavy / big / large fine, не a strong fine. Face a fine — штраф загрожує; pay a fine — його платять.

items.pattern: face / get the death penalty (for sth) · abolish the death penalty · = capital punishment
items.meaning: be in a situation where the punishment could be death
items.example: In the 18th century, a person could **face the death penalty** for stealing a sheep.
more: Nobody in the European Union can **face the death penalty** today.
The documentary is about a man who **faced the death penalty** for a crime he didn't commit.
items.watchOut: «Смертна кара» — the death penalty або capital punishment, не death punishment.

items.pattern: act as / serve as a deterrent (to sb / against sth) · a strong / effective deterrent
items.meaning: make people decide not to do something because they are worried about what will happen
items.example: The cameras outside the shop **act as a deterrent** to shoplifters.
more: A barking dog can **act as a** good **deterrent** against burglars.
Fines for dropping litter **act as a deterrent**, but only if people actually get them.
items.watchOut: Deterrent — те, що відлякує від поганого вчинку. Не плутай з detergent — мийний засіб. Наголос — на другому складі.

items.pattern: suffer / face / take the consequences (of sth)
items.meaning: have to deal with the bad results of something you did
items.example: If you don't pay your parking tickets, sooner or later you'll **suffer the consequences**.
more: We ignored the weather forecast and **suffered the consequences**: we got soaked.
Students who copy their essays from others will **suffer the consequences**.
items.watchOut: «Нести наслідки» — suffer / face / bear the consequences, зазвичай не carry the consequences. Consequences — наслідки; conclusions — висновки.

items.pattern: a harsh / severe / heavy sentence, penalty or punishment · give sb a harsh sentence · opposite: a light sentence
items.meaning: a very severe punishment, often more severe than people think is fair
items.example: Many people thought two years in prison was **a harsh sentence** for a first offence.
more: Some countries have **harsh penalties** for dropping litter in the street.
Many people thought a year's driving ban was **a harsh penalty** for one speeding offence.
items.watchOut: «Суворий вирок» — a harsh / severe / heavy sentence, не a strong sentence. Sentence тут — вирок, а не речення.

items.pattern: a hard / long / difficult legal battle (with / against sb, over sth) · fight a legal battle
items.meaning: a long and difficult fight in the courts
items.example: The two brothers are in **a hard legal battle** over their father's house.
more: Getting compensation from the airline meant **a hard legal battle** that lasted three years.
The small café is facing **a hard legal battle** with a big coffee chain over its name.
items.watchOut: Legal battle — «судова боротьба»: legal тут означає «пов'язаний із законом і судом». Juridical — рідкісне книжне слово, у цьому значенні так не кажуть.

items.pattern: win / lose a case (against sb) · win your case · a court case
items.meaning: get the decision you want from a court
items.example: My neighbour **won her case** against the energy company and got £500 back.
more: The family took the builder to court, but they didn't **win their case**.
Lawyers who **win** a lot of **cases** can charge more.
items.watchOut: Справа в суді — a case, не process і не affair. Судовий процес — a trial.

warmup.uk: Він порушив закон, навіть не знаючи про це.
warmup.q: He ___ the law without even knowing it.
warmup.explain: Порушити закон — break the law. Disturb — турбувати, заважати.

warmup.uk: Минулого тижня парламент ухвалив новий закон про паркування.
warmup.q: Last week Parliament ___ a new law on parking.
warmup.explain: Ухвалити (прийняти) закон — pass a law, не take a law.

warmup.uk: У нашій родині всі дотримуються правил дорожнього руху.
warmup.q: In our family, everyone ___ the rules of the road.
warmup.explain: Дотримуватися правил — follow (або obey, keep to) the rules. Fulfil кажуть про вимоги й обіцянки.

warmup.uk: Поліція проводить розслідування пожежі на складі.
warmup.q: The police are ___ an investigation into the fire at the warehouse.
warmup.explain: Проводити розслідування — carry out (або conduct) an investigation. Take і give з investigation не вживають.

warmup.uk: Присяжним знадобилося три дні, щоб винести вердикт.
warmup.q: It took the jury three days to ___ a verdict.
warmup.explain: Винести вердикт — reach (або return) a verdict.

warmup.uk: Водієві довелося заплатити великий штраф за перевищення швидкості.
warmup.q: The driver had to pay a ___ fine for speeding.
warmup.explain: Великий штраф — a heavy (big, large) fine. Strong fine — калька з «сильний».

warmup.uk: У деяких країнах за контрабанду наркотиків досі загрожує смертна кара.
warmup.q: In some countries, people can still face the death ___ for smuggling drugs.
warmup.explain: Смертна кара — the death penalty (або capital punishment). Death punishment — калька.

warmup.uk: Без хорошого адвоката справу не виграти.
warmup.q: You can't win the ___ without a good lawyer.
warmup.explain: Справа в суді — a case. Process у цьому значенні — калька; судовий процес — trial.

A.q: It's not just bad manners: if you smoke on the train, you're ___ the law.
A.explain: Порушувати закон — break the law. Disturb — турбувати, spoil — псувати.

A.q: Journalists must act ___ the law, even when they're chasing a big story.
A.explain: В межах закону — within the law. In the frames of — калька з «в рамках».

A.q: The police are there to ___ the law, not to make it.
A.explain: Забезпечувати дотримання закону — enforce (або uphold) the law. Force — змушувати, hold up — затримувати.

B.q: The rules don't ___ students to use their phones during the test.
B.explain: Allow / permit sb to do sth. Let — без to (let students use), а give sb to do — калька.

B.q: Taxis in the city must ___ with strict rules about cleanliness and safety.
B.explain: Comply with the rules — дотримуватися правил. Obey вживають без with, а answer тут не підходить.

B.q: The library closes at six, but the librarian ___ the rules and let me stay ten more minutes.
B.explain: Bend the rules — трохи відступити від правил, зробити виняток.

C.q: Everyone accused of a crime has the right to ___ trial.
C.explain: Справедливий суд — a fair trial. Honest trial — калька з «чесний суд».

C.q: Some people think that long prison sentences ___ as a deterrent; others say they don't.
C.explain: Act as a deterrent — стримувати, відлякувати. Можна й serve as a deterrent.

C.q: A lifetime ban from the swimming pool for running? That seems a very ___ penalty.
C.explain: Суворе покарання — a harsh (severe, heavy) penalty. Strong тут — калька з «сильний».

example.title: Tom's parking ticket
example.uk:
Минулої весни наша міська рада запровадила нові правила паркування на нашій вулиці. Правила стосуються всіх, і вони забороняють паркуватися на тротуарі. Більшість сусідів дотримується правил, але якось увечері Том із сусіднього будинку залишив машину наполовину на тротуарі. Через тиждень прийшов лист: йому загрожував великий штраф.

Том був певен, що діяв у межах закону. Власні правила ради вимагають, щоб на кожному кінці вулиці стояв знак, а там був лише один. Він відмовився платити, тож зрештою йому довелося постати перед судом.

Після важкої судової боротьби, яка тривала чотири місяці, Том виграв справу. Тепер там стоять два нові знаки, а Том паркується у своєму гаражі.
example.en:
Last spring our council [[introduced|a3]] new parking rules for our street. The rules [[apply to|b3]] everyone, and they [[prohibit|b1]] parking on the pavement. Most neighbours [[follow the rules|b4]], but one evening Tom from next door left his car half on the pavement. A week later, a letter arrived: he [[was facing a heavy fine|c7]].

Tom was sure he had [[acted within the law|a4]]. The council's own regulations [[require|b5]] a sign at each end of the street, and there was only one. He refused to pay, so in the end he had to [[appear in court|c2]].

After a [[hard legal battle|c12]] that lasted four months, Tom [[won his case|c13]]. Now there are two new signs, and he parks in his garage.
